bib.title: OpenCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents

legacy_report:
SOURCE: OpenCUA: Open Foundations for Computer-Use Agents. Xinyuan Wang, Bowen Wang, Dunjie Lu, Junlin Yang, Tianbao Xie, Junli Wang et al. (XLANG Lab HKU, Moonshot AI, Stanford, Waterloo, CMU; senior author Tao Yu). NeurIPS 2025 (39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems), arXiv:2508.09123v3, 4 Oct 2025.

COVERAGE: All 44 pages extracted, 138,308 chars, all read. Body, limitations, Table 11 results, error study and appendix A-E in full. Case-study trajectory (App. F) and training-data examples (App. G, pp. 30-44) are step-by-step transcripts and were only skimmed, plus the tail. References skimmed. No extraction faults except garbled table columns and spaced-out text in App. G. Figures were not rendered; I used the extracted captions and plot numbers.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- OpenCUA-72B reaches 45.0% on OSWorld-Verified at a 100-step budget, best among open-source models and level with Claude 4 Sonnet.
  number: 45.0% (100 steps)
  setup: Qwen2.5-VL-72B SFT. Stage 1 is 250B tokens and Stage 2 is 16B tokens. Data is AgentNet plus 8k Ubuntu rollouts from o3+Jedi. L2 CoT inference, temperature 0, OSWorld-Verified average of 3 runs, 1920x1080, run by the OSWorld team on AWS.
  quote: "OPENCUA-72B reaches 45.0 % in 100 steps, establishing a new state-of-the-art among open-source systems, closing the gap from open-source models to Claude models."
  where: p.9 (Sec 4.2); Table 3, p.10
- Table 3 gives the baselines at 15/50/100 steps. Open source: UI-TARS-72B-DPO 24.0/25.8/27.1, Qwen3-VL 38.1 at 100, Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct 4.4/-/5.0, Kimi-VL-A3B 9.7/-/10.3. Proprietary: OpenAI CUA 26.0/31.3/31.4, Claude 4 Sonnet 31.2/43.9/41.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5 61.4 at 100. OpenCUA-7B 24.3/28.1/26.6, OpenCUA-32B 29.7/34.1/34.8, OpenCUA-72B 39.0/44.9/45.0.
  quote: "Claude Sonnet 4.5 achieves 61.4 % at 100 steps, followed by Claude 4 Sonnet at 43.9 %." Table 3 rows: "OpenCUA-32B (Ours)29.7 +0.8−1.5 34.1+1.0−0.6 34.8+0.9−1.0", "OpenCUA-72B (Ours)39.0 44.9 45.0 +1.1−1.2"
  where: p.9-10. Note Claude 4 Sonnet's 43.9 is at 50 steps and 41.5 at 100, so 72B's 45.0 beats that 100-step figure. The text says "comparable". Sonnet 4.5 (61.4) is well ahead.
- Reflective long CoT improves OSWorld success from 11.5 to 15.3. Mixed L1/L2/L3 CoT training beats L2 only (18.5 vs 13.1). The same ablation table also gives the test-time format results: L1 16.9, L2 18.5, L3 17.6.
  number: 11.5 -> 15.3 (+3.8 points)
  setup: Qwen2-VL-7B, 14K Win&Mac + 3K Ubuntu trajectories, OSWorld at 15 steps. "Without reflective long CoT" means the Aguvis-style short CoT.
  quote: "In Figure 6, we see that reflective long CoT improves the performance from 11.5 to 15.3." Table 6: "Reflective Long CoT Short-CoT 11.5Advanced-CoT 15.3"
  where: p.14 (Sec 5, Table 6). The paper only conjectures that self-correction explains the gain.
- Base recipe (state-action pairs only, no reasoning) is poor: direct fine-tuning on the trajectories gives 4.4% on OSWorld.
  number: 4.4%
  quote: "directly finetuning vision-language action (VLA) models on our 27K trajectories leads to poor performance (4.4% success rate on OSWorld [46], shown in Figure 1 Left "Base Recipe")."
  where: p.5 (Sec 3). Footnote 1: 41,428 trajectories trained OpenCUA-7B/32B and 27,804 trained OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B/A3B.
- AgentNet dataset: 22,625 human-annotated desktop tasks, 3 OSes, avg 18.6 steps.
  number: 22,625 tasks; about 12K Windows, 5K macOS, 5K Ubuntu; 140+ apps, 190 websites
  setup: Collected with AgentNetTool on annotators' own machines; each task must be over 15 steps (under 5 is rejected). The abstract says 3 OSes and 200+ apps and websites.
  quote: "Our dataset consists of 22,625 human-annotated computer-use tasks, including 12K from Windows, 5K from macOS and 5K from Ubuntu... Each trajectory averages 18.6 steps" and "the data spans over 140 applications and 190 websites"
  where: p.5 (Sec 2.3). The intro says "over 100 applications and 200 websites". The two counts are inconsistent in the paper.
- Cost: annotating 22K tasks took 6 months and about USD 20,000. CoT synthesis cost USD 0.6 per task (claude-3-7-sonnet). Total is about USD 32,000. Annotation speed is about ten tasks per hour, with 634 part-time annotators.
  quote: "The total annotation cost was about USD 20,000... The total cost of building this dataset is about USD 32,000."
  where: p.26 (C.2)
- Data scaling is consistent. Combined OSWorld goes 9.8 -> 18.5 as data grows from 7K Ubuntu to 10K Ubuntu + 17K Win&Mac. Win&Mac data helps OSWorld even though it is out of domain. In-domain Ubuntu 3K to 10K gives +72% average, and Win&Mac 3K to 14K gives +125%.
  setup: Qwen2-VL-7B. Figure 7 shows OSWorld, WindowsAgentArena and AgentNetBench.
  quote: "On OSWorld, performance improves significantly from9.8%to18.5%, despite the added Win&Mac data coming from a different platform." and "When increasing the Ubuntu data from 3K to 10K, the average performance improves by 72%. Scaling the Win/Mac data from 3K to 14K yields a 125% improvement on average."
  where: p.11-12
- Pass@k headroom is large. OpenCUA-72B goes 45.0 (Pass@1) -> 53.2 (Pass@3). OpenCUA-32B goes 34.2 -> 45.6 (Pass@3).
  setup: OSWorld-Verified, 3 runs, 100 steps for the 72B. Table 11 lists 32B Pass@3 as 45.58% at 50 steps and 45.10% at 100 steps. The 72B Pass@3 is 53.02% in the table (labelled 100 steps).
  quote: "Pass@3 success rate of OPENCUA-32B on OSWORLD-Verified jumps from 34.2%(Pass@1) to45.6%. The performance of OPENCUA-72B increases from 45.0%(Pass@ 1)to53.2%(Pass@ 3)."
  where: p.10; Table 11, p.28. Minor internal mismatch: the text says 53.2 and the table says 53.02.
- Pass@16 on a small model: OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B at temperature 0.1 on OSWorld goes from 16.9 to 34.6 (+104%) at 15 steps and from 18.4 to 39.2 (+113%) at 50 steps. The step-budget gain grows with n. Higher temperature raises Pass@n but lowers Pass@1.
  quote: "On 15 step, the success rate increases from 16.9 to 34.6 (+104%), while on 50 step, the increacement is even large from 18.4 to 39.2 (+113%)."
  where: p.12 (Fig 8). The text cites "Table 8", which is a mislabel for Fig 8.
- At temperature 0, Pass@16 on OSWorld is 38.60% vs Pass@1 20.10% at 50 steps (OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B). Small perturbations such as the system date change outcomes.
  quote: "The curves for Pass@16 (38.60% SR at 50 steps) and Pass@1 (20.10% SR) demonstrate a >18% absolute gap"
  where: p.12-13 (Fig 9)
- Step-budget effect: gains from 15 to 50 steps exceed gains from 50 to 100. For the 32B, 29.7 -> 34.1 -> 34.8. Base models gain under 1%. Claude 4 Sonnet goes +12.7% from 15 to 50, then -2.4% from 50 to 100.
  quote: "OPENCUA-32B: +4.4 % (29.7 → 34.1) from 15 → 50 steps, and +0.7 % (34.1 → 34.8) from 50→100 steps."
  where: p.9. The authors blame error loops and failure to stop.
- Grounding: 72B gets 60.8% on ScreenSpot-Pro and 37.3% on UI-Vision (SOTA). 32B gets 59.6 on OSWorld-G, 55.3 on ScreenSpot-Pro, 93.4 on ScreenSpot-V2 and 33.3 on UI-Vision. 7B gets 55.3 / 50.0 / 92.3 / 29.7.
  quote: "OPENCUA-72B achieves60.8% on ScreenSpot-Pro and37.3% (SOTA) on UI-Vision."
  where: p.11 (Table 5). Grounding alone is not enough: OpenCUA-A3B scores 19.9% and OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B scores 23.0% on OSWorld.
- Other model sizes. OpenCUA-7B (joint training, 200B tokens) reaches 27.3% on OSWorld online. Table 11 average is 26.67% at 100 steps. OpenCUA-A3B and OpenCUA-Qwen2-7B are single runs: A3B 16.90/19.94/17.73 and Qwen2-7B 19.94/20.61/23.06 at 15/50/100 steps.
  quote: "achieving 27.3% success rate on OSWorld Online Evaluation Platform."
  where: p.8; Table 11 p.28
- Test-time format: L2 (thought + action) is best at inference, 18.5 vs L1 16.9 and L3 17.6, contrary to Aguvis and UI-TARS. History: L1 action text plus 3 screenshots is the default. 1/3/5 images give about 6.5/9.6/9.9 (read from the Fig 10 extraction, not quoted prose). Going from 3 to 5 images adds about 3K context tokens for little gain.
  quote: "increasing from 3 to 5 images yields marginal gains while incurring 3K more context tokens and delayed convergence"
  where: p.13
- General text data gives a small gain, with 35% general text in the mix. 15 steps 18.5 vs 17.5 and 50 steps 20.1 vs 19.1 (as read from the extraction, with and without text).
  quote: "the general text data slightly improves model's agentic performance"
  where: p.14 (Fig 11)
- AgentNetBench (offline, 100 held-out Win/macOS tasks, multiple valid actions per step): Avg SR OpenCUA-32B 79.1, OpenCUA-7B 75.2, OpenAI CUA 73.1, Qwen2.5-VL-72B 67.0. It correlates with online success at a 15-step budget (power-law fit).
  quote: "OpenCUA-32B (Ours)81.9 66.155.7 79.1"
  where: Table 4, p.11; App. B p.22-23. OpenAI CUA is stronger on terminate detection (80.0 vs 55.7).
- Training recipes. Stage-2-only uses 70% CUA and 30% general data. 32B Stage 2 uses 45% planning and 20% grounding. Joint training uses 20/20/60 with 3 epochs on multi-image data. Hardware reached 480 x A100 for the 72B. Qwen2-VL-7B ran 96 x A100 for about 45 h. Jointly trained OpenCUA-7B took 8 days on 128 A100s.
  where: p.7-8

LIMITS
- Authors concede (App. A): dataset scale is bounded by human annotation. Annotators are not experts and may avoid shortcuts or scripts. Consent requirements bring selection bias.
- Error study (App. E): lack of app knowledge (VLOOKUP, bulk fill), imprecise grounding (subscripting "2" in H2O), action repetition loops, wrong termination, failure on tasks needing 30-50+ gold actions, and weak error perception and recovery.
- Online variance is high. Pass@1 vs Pass@16 gaps exceed 18 points even at temperature 0, so single-run numbers are noisy. Only OSWorld-Verified results for 7B/32B/72B are averaged over 3 runs. Ablations are on small 7B models with single runs, so differences of 1-4 points have no confidence intervals.
- Reflective CoT is generated by claude-3-7-sonnet, so the "open" recipe depends on a proprietary teacher. The 72B also used 8k o3+Jedi rollouts.
- Proprietary models still lead. Sonnet 4.5 is at 61.4, versus 45.0 for OpenCUA-72B. The comparison table mixes sources and step budgets.
- Dated. Qwen3-VL (38.1) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 appear as late additions. As of 2025 the work is SFT only; the paper covers no RL.
- Desktop only, screenshot-based. No latency or real-time analysis. No safety evaluation, despite the motivation.

BUILDS ON: Aguvis (Xu et al. 2024) for the L1/L2/L3 CoT and two-stage grounding then planning curriculum. ActRe (Yang et al. 2024) and ReAct (Yao et al. 2023) for reasoning plus acting. V* (Wu & Xie 2023) for the zoomed-in patch visual cues. DuckTrack (TheDuckAI) and OpenAdapt for input capture, OBS Studio for recording, and OSWorld (Xie et al. 2024) for axtree parsing and the benchmark. UI-TARS (Qin et al. 2025). Jedi (Xie et al. 2025). Base models Qwen2-VL, Qwen2.5-VL and Kimi-VL (Kimi Team 2025). WindowsAgentArena (Bonatti et al. 2024). Grounding data from ShowUI and UGround. Compared against OS-Genesis, AgentTrek, AndroidControl and others (Table 2).

CODE: none. Action space (Table 1, p.3) is a PyAutoGUI subset: click(x,y,button), middleClick, doubleClick, tripleClick, moveTo, dragTo, scroll(dx,dy), hscroll, write(text), press(key), hotkey(key1,key2), wait(), terminate('success' or 'failure'). Example output format (App. F): "Code: pyautogui.click(x=0.988, y=0.081)", with coordinates normalised to 0-1.

FIGURES (from extracted captions and text, not rendered)
- Fig 1 (p.1): OSWorld-Verified. Left: data and model scaling, base recipe vs the OpenCUA recipe. Right: 72B vs open-source models and Claude 4 Sonnet. The headline plot.
- Fig 2 (p.2): framework overview, tool, trajectory processing, dataset and bench, models.
- Fig 5/6 (p.6): reflective long-CoT pipeline (reflector, generator, summarizer) and a worked reflection example. Explains the method faster than prose.
- Fig 7 (p.12): scaling curves by OS domain (3K to 14K) on OSWorld, WAA and AgentNetBench.
- Fig 8/9 (p.12-13): Pass@N curves at temperature 0.1 and 0. Fig 10: history ablation. Fig 11: text data ablation. Fig 13: offline vs online correlation (fit 16.813x^1.913).

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found. Table 3 extraction has "61,4" (a comma typo) for 61.4. The Table 11 Pass@3 rows have merged numbers (e.g. "Pass@3 10053.02%19.01", meaning step budget 100 then 53.02%). Table and figure references are mislabelled in places ("Table 8" for Fig 8, "Figure 5" for Pass@n). Figure 6's numbers 11.5/15.3 come from Table 6 text. Figure 11 and Figure 10 values were inferred from axis labels in the extraction. App. F/G transcripts were not read line by line.
